I need to choose between paying the $50 jail fine or rolling for doubles.

Opponent p2 has a dangerous orange and dark blue monopoly with heavy rents. I have a light blue monopoly and several mortgaged properties.

I already rolled once and failed to get doubles. I have one more chance before the mandatory $50 fine.

I will stay in jail. I can collect rent from their landings while avoiding their dangerous properties. I am calculating the light blue rent values.

Oriental Avenue with four houses pays $400. That would bankrupt the opponent immediately. Vermont and Connecticut pay $270 and $300 respectively. These are too high to ignore. Staying in jail is the only safe choice.

Rolling for doubles would let me leave jail and move 2 through 12 spaces. I am checking which board positions I would land on from the jail space.

Rolling doubles from jail would land me on St. Charles, Virginia, or St. James. St. James is owned by the opponent with four houses, so that would be dangerous. The other two positions are mortgaged and pay no rent.

Rolling doubles from jail would also land me on New York Avenue with four houses, paying $800. Free Parking is safe and Chance is risky.

Dark blue properties pay $1100 and $1400 with three houses. I cannot survive those either. Rolling doubles is a 1 in 6 chance. Only a roll of 2, 4, or 10 is safe.
